root_idea.summary: The root denotes turning or placing a thing upside down, with its former upper or forward position reversed.
root_idea.development: From physical inversion, the lexicon develops senses of reversal into a former state, relapse, decline from strength into weakness or old age, lowered posture, defective orientation, and figurative baseness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested Form I passive verb, normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
Distinct Quran-attested Form II verb, normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
Distinct Quran-attested active participle; the supplied plural Quran form is presented under the supported singular citation form.

senses.definition: To be turned upside down or reversed, with the former order or position inverted.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the passive Quranic construction ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلَى رُؤُوسِهِمْ, literally portraying a turning upon the head.

senses.definition: To be turned back to a former position or state, especially to revert from recognized truth to disputation or disbelief.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic construction uses the image of being turned back after having reached a sound course or recognized the evidence.

senses.definition: To reverse a person's constitution through aging, bringing strength and youthfulness into weakness and extreme old age.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use describes the causative reversal produced by prolonged life; it is the Form II counterpart of being reduced from an earlier state.

senses.definition: Lowering or hanging the head, with the head bowed toward the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence presents the participle in a plural human context of abasement or humiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or put something upside down, reverse it, or change its state, sometimes with an intensive force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the broader Form II lexical use apart from the specifically Quranic aging construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relapse into an illness after convalescence or incomplete recovery; of a wound, to break open or become active again; causatively, to make a disease return.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be the person or wound that relapses, or food and another cause that brings the illness back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an imprecation, to fall upon the face and not rise before suffering a second fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the formula تَعْسًا لَهُ وَنُكْسًا, with نَكْسًا also reported as a dialectal or formally harmonized variant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply dye to the head repeatedly or several times.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A repeated-action use applied to the process of putting dye on the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak or impotent, or to fall short of one's fellows and be unable to attain them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical usage describing reduced capacity or failure to reach the level of one's peers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend, lower, stoop, or hang the head toward the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe simple inclination or lowering caused by abasement; the Form VIII expression انْتَكَسَ is also equated with this use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become overturned, inverted, or reversed; literally, to fall upon one's head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive or intransitive Form VIII development of the turning-over idea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be disappointed in attaining one's desire and suffer loss.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative imprecation associated with being overthrown in one's affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow whose upper or notched part has broken, leaving it turned bottom-for-top; also an arrowhead or blade defective in this way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The defining feature is the reversal of the arrow's intended upper and lower orientation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow whose foot is made from the head of the branch, a defective construction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of a bow with its parts arranged in the faulty reversed manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A child born feet first, with the feet emerging before the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare obstetric expression; the evidence itself records qualification concerning its established authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low, base, mean, or sordid person; by extension, one weak or falling short in courage, generosity, or attainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application derived from the defective or inferior condition associated with نِكْسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very old men tottering because of extreme age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural lexical use associated with advanced age and physical unsteadiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that does not raise its head or neck while running because of weakness, or that fails to keep pace with the other horses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine description of weakness, impotence, or failure to reach the other runners.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A circumambulation of the Kaaba performed contrary to the prescribed custom, saluting the Black Stone and then proceeding toward the left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized ritual expression describing an inverted or non-prescribed order of circumambulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Recited or read backwards, beginning with the last part and proceeding toward the first, or from the end of a chapter toward its beginning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to Quran recitation performed in an inverted order; the cited discussion distinguishes reported variants and notes limited instructional allowances.
